citation.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Mechanical Component Design Based on Topology Optimization Considering the Restrictions of Additive Manufacturing
citation.authors: Abid Ullah; Karim Asami; Lukas Holtz; Tim Röver; Kashif Azher; Katharina Bartsch; Claus Emmelmann
citation.venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing 8(5), 220
citation.version_coded: version of record, publisher PDF host

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the cantilever example, one ToPy topology optimization averages 90 seconds, while the trained image generator is said to produce a candidate in milliseconds.
claim.location: Section 2, methodology, paragraph after ToPy/SIMP description
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 2 reports 90 s for ToPy but gives only an order of magnitude ('milliseconds') for ML inference, so an exact ratio cannot be derived.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Section 6 claim eliminating iterative TO steps and lowering development costs; Section 6 reports up to 91% artefact-free reliability relative to TO-generated reference images.

baseline.hardware_classical: 12-core processor, model not stated; one ToPy run uses about 25% CPU (Section 2)
baseline.problem_size: 2D cantilever image/grid resolution not stated in the timing comparison (Section 2)
baseline.classical_time: 90 s average for one ToPy optimization (Section 2); 250 h for 10,000 training designs serially or 62.5 h with four concurrent runs
baseline.ml_time: milliseconds per candidate after training, no exact value (Sections 1-2)
baseline.training_time: not stated separately; Section 2 calls the 250 h dataset-generation time a one-time model-training cost
baseline.data_generation_cost: 10,000 ToPy optimizations: 250 h serial or 62.5 h with four concurrent runs (Section 2)
baseline.quality_metric: Pixel-by-pixel image deviation from ToPy outputs and visual artefact inspection (Section 3.2)
baseline.quality_gap: Up to 91% artefact-free reliability (abstract and Section 6); Section 3.2 notes examples with 4.04% image deviation can be structurally poor and 10.8% deviation can still be meaningful

R1.evidence: Section 2 compares 90 s ToPy runtime with millisecond image generation, while Section 3.2 validates only image similarity and explicitly says returned designs were not mechanically checked by FEM.

R2.evidence: Section 2 uses Python ToPy and says one run consumes only 25% of the 12-core processor, with no direct comparison to an efficient classical solver on comparable hardware.

R3.evidence: Section 2 reports 250 h serial or 62.5 h parallel to generate 10,000 training pairs but does not separately report network training time or a break-even number of uses.

R4.evidence: Section 3.2 validates returned designs with pixel comparisons and visual inspection; it explicitly states that FEM mechanical validation was not performed.

reporting.n_test_cases: 100 test image pairs for Model 4 and 200 for Model 5 (Section 3.1); seven model setups (Table 1)

notes: Section 3.1 reports nine incomplete/artefact outputs among 100 Model 4 tests and 32 disconnected or strongly artefact outputs among 200 Model 5 tests. Its image-based success rate is not mechanical feasibility. Figure 16 reports standard deviations across image results, but no random-seed variability.
